human_tolerance.notes: 'The eastern chipmunk lives in deciduous wooded areas and urban parks throughout the eastern United States and southern Canada', and it prefers 'locations with rocky areas, brush or log piles, and shrubs to provide cover'. Domestic dogs and cats are listed among its predators.

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: "During the winter, the chipmunk may enter long periods of hibernation." The dormancy is not obligate, so the temperature and duration thresholds in seasonal.triggers are authored judgement, since no open source states them.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: First of two breeding seasons, February to April.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Second breeding season, June to August.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Females usually produce one or two litters of three to five young a year; pups stay with their mothers for around six to eight weeks after birth.

phases.name: moult
phases.note: Moulting occurs once or twice a year, in May or June and sometimes again in October.

vocalizations.description: The 'chip', one of five stereotyped sounds in the species' vocal repertoire, and the commonest contact note between individuals.
The 'chuck', a low, harsh note in the same five-sound repertoire, given in alarm and in the sharp chatter an agitated chipmunk produces.
The trill, a rapid rolling rattle measured at 130 trills per minute - the one quantified figure in the species' vocal repertoire.
A high whistle or squeal, given when a chipmunk is startled or a predator is close; with the chip and the chuck it is one of the five stereotyped sounds of the repertoire.

taxonomy.note: The genus was changed from Sciurus to Tamias by Illiger in 1811, per the article's Etymology section.

range.note: The article is thin on range: 'a chipmunk species found in eastern North America', with the habitat section adding 'throughout the eastern United States and southern Canada'. That supports US and CA as the native range and nothing more; no introduced range is described. A reviewer wanting the county-level detail should note that the source does not carry it.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: "The eastern chipmunk can climb trees well, but constructs underground nests with extensive tunnel systems", and it forages on the ground for most of the day.

traits.perching.note: Climbs well and forages in shrubs, but does not perch on a branch the way a bird does; set to false, matching the treatment of sciurus-carolinensis and sciurus-niger.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits MamFuncDat BodyMass-Value 111.91 g, near the middle of Wikipedia's 66-150 g range.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia's 'about 30 cm (12 in) in length including the tail'. The figure is given as an approximation in the source, so it is recorded as stated rather than as a midpoint of a range.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Judgement: the article gives total length including tail but no shoulder height and no hind-foot length, so there is nothing to compute from. 0.11 m is a scale-consistent estimate for a 30 cm chipmunk standing on its hind limbs. The field is optional and the validator asks for it on a quadruped; a measured value would replace it.

traits.lifespan_y.note: "On average, eastern chipmunks live three or more years in the wild, but in captivity they may live as long as eight years."

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Seed 30, Diet-PlantO 30, Diet-Fruit 20 and Diet-Inv 20 give the fractions directly, with Diet-PlantO mapped to the schema's browse for the bulbs and green plants the article names. The article's mushrooms, worms and bird eggs are folded into the browse and invertebrate shares rather than carried separately, since the schema diet has no fungi key and the sourced fractions already total 100.

traits.social.note: "The eastern chipmunk defends its burrow and lives a solitary life, except during mating season", and it is solitary for the six to eight weeks its pups spend with the mother, so group_size tops out at 2.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Activity-Diurnal 1 with Nocturnal and Crepuscular 0, and the article's 'The chipmunk is mainly active during the day, spending most of its day foraging' agree exactly.

traits.defense.note: "The eastern chipmunk defends its burrow" - with a network of tunnels and several entrances, and burrows further disguised by lining them with leaves, rocks and sticks, its answer to a threat is to get into the tunnel system.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.35. It lives in urban parks and gardens and habituates to people, but bolts for its burrow at any approach and domestic cats and dogs are listed among its predators.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value 'G' gives the ground stratum, matching the article's underground nest and day-long ground foraging; the 0.25 arboreal share reflects 'can climb trees well' and foraging in shrubs, but no source quantifies the split.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet exactly. Nesting weight is entirely on the burrow. log_pile and leaf_litter carry the cover the habitat section names - 'rocky areas, brush or log piles, and shrubs' plus the leaves, rocks and sticks the burrow is lined with - and are weighted by judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'Urban parks' is named alongside deciduous woodland as where it lives, and the cover it prefers - brush, log piles and shrubs - is what a garden and its edges provide. impervious_max, flight_distance_m and road_mortality are authored judgement and are not quantified in the source; domestic cats and dogs being listed as predators is the one human-related datum the article gives.

habitat.density_per_ha.note: Judgement: no open source gives a density. A chipmunk defends a small burrow system and forages over a compact patch of ground and shrubs, giving typical 1 per hectare, and min and max are an authored tenfold band either side, following the convention used for turdus-migratorius and sciurus-carolinensis.

seasonal.strategy.note: "During the winter, the chipmunk may enter long periods of hibernation." Hibernation is the schema's strategy for that; the caveat is that it is not obligate, which is why the winter dormancy is expressed as a phase with a window rather than a whole-year state.

seasonal.triggers.note: Authored judgement, flagged as such: the schema requires triggers for a Hibernation strategy and no open source states the weather that starts and ends it for this species. Two weeks below 0 C to enter and a week above 5 C to exit are plausible for a small hibernating rodent in a Michigan winter, and should be replaced if a sourced figure appears.

seasonal.phases.note: Winter hibernation, the February-April and June-August breeding seasons, one or two litters of three to five young a year, the six to eight weeks pups spend with the mother, and moulting once or twice a year in May or June and sometimes October are all stated in the article.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration is the article's own 'around six to eight weeks' after birth, taken at its midpoint of 56 days. scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: The five stereotyped sounds - the chip, the chuck, the trills, the whistle or squeal, and chatter - are quoted directly from the article, as is the measured trill rate of 130 trills per minute. Contexts are assigned from that list and from the squeal's stated alarm role; time windows and cooldowns are authored judgement, since no open source quantifies them. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

look.note: Colours from the Description: reddish-brown fur on the upper body, five dark brown stripes contrasting with light brown stripes along the back ending in a dark tail, lighter fur on the lower body, a tawny stripe running from the whiskers to below the ears, and light stripes over the eyes. The back stripe and eye stripe parts render the two most diagnostic markings and the cheek pouches render what the species is named for. Proportions are authored judgement for a small, low-slung, short-tailed rodent with four toes in front and five behind. No open source describes the eye colour, so eye is a judgement value. The light stripe over the eye was dropped and the cheek pouch cut to a small bulge: at full size both boxes projected past the head and the previewer showed a cluster of pale boxes rather than an animal. The cheek pouch is kept because it is what the species is named for.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program. food_tag is seed because seeds and nuts are a third of the sourced diet and are what it hoards; rest_sun_lo_deg and rest_sun_hi_deg set to -90 and -6 per the program's description for a diurnal species, which EltonTraits and Wikipedia both confirm; flee_m 5 m, calm_m 15 m and food_m 15 m are scaled down from the fox-squirrel example for a much smaller animal with a small defended home range, with flee_gait gallop for the dash back to the burrow.
